stem: Which four things share the context window?
options: Model weights, tokeniser, sampler and cache
System prompt, conversation history, retrieved/attached content, and the answer
Only the user's message and the answer
explanation: One fixed budget, four claimants. Grow the first three and the answer is squeezed — unless you decide what to drop.

stem: You leave 120 tokens of room and the model needs 800 to answer. What happens?
options: A truncated answer or an error — reserve output room explicitly
The model compresses the answer to fit
explanation: The answer reserve is the part people forget. Set max_tokens deliberately and budget for it.

stem: The example drops oldest history first, then least-relevant documents. Why never the system prompt?
options: It is always the shortest part
It carries the rules and tool definitions the whole request depends on
explanation: A policy is a choice for your product; keeping instructions and answer reserve intact is almost always right. Log what you dropped.

stem: What is wrong with letting the API or your framework truncate an oversized prompt for you?
options: You do not know what was dropped, so wrong answers cannot be traced to missing context
It costs more than truncating yourself
It always drops the system prompt
explanation: Truncation you did not choose is a silent bug. Measure, reserve, apply a policy, log.

stem: A 200k-token window fits all 40 documents. What is the strongest reason not to send them all every request?
options: Cost and latency scale with tokens sent, and quality does not scale with volume — the middle gets lost
explanation: Long context is a capacity, not a strategy. Retrieval exists so you can send less (Module 6).

stem: Why does the example use ~4 characters per token, and what should production do instead?
options: It is exact for all languages
It is a portable rule of thumb; production should count with the model's real tokeniser
explanation: Code, JSON and non-English text can differ by 2–3×. Count with the tokeniser you will be billed by (Lesson 2.2).

stem: Where should the key question go in a long prompt, given attention behaviour?
options: At the end (with instructions at the start); bulk material in between
explanation: Start and end are attended to more reliably than the middle. Instructions first, question last.

stem: Which of these silently consumes context that engineers often forget to count?
options: Tool schemas and few-shot examples in the system prompt
explanation: A dozen verbosely described tools can eat thousands of tokens before the user says a word.

stem: Summarising the entire conversation every turn to save tokens costs…
options: An extra generation call per turn (input = whole history) and a full round-trip of latency; summarise only past a threshold instead
explanation: The recap is itself an LLM call. Keep the last N turns verbatim and summarise older ones when history exceeds a threshold.

stem: Which log line best supports diagnosing a truncated answer?
options: tokens: system=900 history=3400 retrieved=6200 reserve=1500 window=16000 dropped=[turn1..turn4] finish_reason=length
explanation: Tokens per part, what was dropped, and the finish reason tell an on-call engineer exactly why the answer was cut (Lesson 5.7).
